approach: Add one shared private const CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE to briefs.rs. Render it in the reader brief as its own `# Checkable criteria` section, after the code survey guide and before `# What the verifier can run`, so READING_RULES, its tests and the existing wording are untouched. Render it in the producer brief as a new `## Make your evidence checkable` section (fn checkable_evidence_section), placed just before criteria_check_section. The producer section is narrow: prefer a test in the change, add a new file only when a deliverable or criterion names it, and if a criterion can be shown only from the report, say so in its criteria_check entry. Two tests render the briefs and assert on their text. In structure-pass.md section 5, every report-held proof becomes something the verifier reruns or reads in the diff or the snapshot (a rerun command, a diff check, or an existing committed test). No evidence file or docs note is added, so items 4 and 7 stay true. One CHANGELOG line. No refusal logic, prompt file or governance file changes.

decisions.choice: New standalone `# Checkable criteria` section in the reader brief, not a ninth READING_RULES line
decisions.reason: READING_RULES is [&str; 8] and tests (~4476-4521) assert len 8, one check named per line, lines <=220 bytes and the section <2600 bytes. The rule adds no check (check_criteria_evidence stays as is). Its own `# ` heading ends the rules section at the next `\n# `, so those tests read the same text.

rejected.why: Breaks the len==8 and 'each rule names a check' assertions and needs edits to existing tests.

rejected.option: Append the sentence to the 'What the verifier can run' paragraph
rejected.why: That section prints only when verifier_can_run is non-empty and an existing test covers its wording; the rule should always show and the existing wording must stay unchanged.

rejected.option: Edit prompts/reader.md or the producer prompt
rejected.why: Reader headroom is 3 tokens, budgets are fixed and prompt files are out of scope.

decisions.choice: The reader section does not point at 'the list below'. It says: write each criterion so its check names a file, a diff line or a command the verifier can run (listed under What the verifier can run when given).
decisions.reason: Finding 5: the list prints only when verifier_can_run is non-empty (briefs.rs:2426), while the new section must always show.

rejected.why: The list can be absent, leaving a dangling reference.

decisions.choice: Narrow producer text. The section carries the shared rule, then: prefer a test in your change that shows the property; add a new file for evidence only when a deliverable or a criterion names it; if a criterion can be shown only from your report, say in its criteria_check entry that the verifier cannot check it, and do not invent a file.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: a blanket 'put proof in a file' would make producers add stray notes files in every job and break file-scope criteria and unchanged_files_section comparisons (briefs.rs:770). Preferring a test and allowing a file only when named avoids false positives.

rejected.option: Tell every producer to commit a counts or notes file for non-diff proof
rejected.why: Stray files break file-scope criteria such as criterion 6.

decisions.choice: Producer wording says 'in your change' / 'in the candidate', never 'commit'
decisions.reason: Finding 4: the working-directory text (briefs.rs:657) says 'Your edits become the candidate' and Athena owns commits.

rejected.why: Contradicts the working-directory text and may prompt git commit attempts.

decisions.choice: One shared private const used by both briefs
decisions.reason: The two briefs cannot drift, and each test asserts the same literal phrase written in the test, not the constant.

rejected.option: Write the rule separately in each brief

decisions.choice: Rewrite every report-held proof in section 5 so the verifier reruns it or reads it in the diff, adding no evidence file: item 2 (--list), item 3 (non-moved lines), item 5 (caller check), the two R5-R8 bullets, the 5.2 'both runs' sentence, plus the report-adjacent 'job names the test' (item 5 tail) and 'job repeats the Grep' (5.2); also the row-294 wording
decisions.reason: Findings 1, 2 and 6. Item 2: the verifier reruns `cargo test --locked -p athena-core -- --list`; item 1 already forbids any test line removed or added except `use` lines in the diff, so names are equal and no count in a report is needed. Item 3: the verifier reads `git diff -M --color-moved=zebra` and every line not marked moved must be a `mod`, `use`, `pub use` or visibility line; the reason is not a report. Item 5: the verifier reruns the Grep for each old path over `crates/` on the candidate; `git diff -U0 -- crates/` must show no line containing an old path removed or added outside moved blocks, and the build compiles every hit; for fake hosts implementing PrHost the existing test named in the 5.1 table is run by name. No docs note is added, so items 4 and 7 (diff-stat limit, no other docs change) stay true. R5-R8: the diff shows each removed `return Ok(closing)` with a `Flow::Stop` added in its place, counted by the verifier from `git diff`; every local that crossed a seam is a named field in the added struct in the diff. 5.2: the guard's own self-tests in external_calls_guard.rs (committed) are run by the verifier on the candidate, and a committed test selects D87 and D88. The 5.1 row 294 becomes 'the early-return pairing read in the diff'.

rejected.option: Item 5: a committed note under docs/ with before/after counts
rejected.why: Items 4 and 7 forbid extra docs changes, and a 'before' count in a note is still the producer's claim the verifier cannot recheck.

rejected.option: Item 5: a test with `use` lines for each old path
rejected.why: Item 1 allows only `use` line changes in tests; adding a new test file or lines for this conflicts with 'same tests, unedited' and the 'no other change' rule.
Leaves item 2, item 3, the R5-R8 bullets and the 5.2 sentence report-only, failing the Grep `report` check.

decisions.choice: No new refusal or matching check
decisions.reason: The request is a stated rule with a test; check_criteria_evidence already refuses criteria citing the report. No refusal_corpus case or refusal-rate change is involved.

rejected.option: Extend check_criteria_evidence to refuse 'change description' wording
rejected.why: Out of scope; needs replay and corpus work.

decisions.choice: Show file scope (criterion 6) with `git diff --stat` and `git status` in the snapshot repository
decisions.reason: Both are in the verifier's allowed commands and list any extra touched file directly.

rejected.why: Tests do not detect an extra edited file.

files.purpose: Add CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE (near VERIFIER_VISIBILITY, ~1060), the reader `# Checkable criteria` section in reader_brief (after CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE, ~2425), fn checkable_evidence_section and its call before criteria_check_section (~686), and two tests.

Section 5: rewrite items 2, 3 and 5, the two R5-R8 bullets, the 5.2 'both runs' and 'repeats the Grep' sentences, and the 5.1 row for R5-R8 so each proof is a rerun, a diff check or an existing committed test; add a one-sentence opening note that no item rests on the report or change description.
One bullet under [Unreleased] ### Added naming the rule in the reader and producer briefs and the section 5 change.

steps: Read briefs.rs around reader_brief (~2256-2440), producer_brief_with_evidence (~626-693) and the test helpers (`reader_inputs` ~4457, `reading()` ~2486, `defaults()` ~2543) to copy their form.

In briefs.rs add `const CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE: &str` after VERIFIER_VISIBILITY (~1066): "Every acceptance criterion must be checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs, never from the producer's report or change description, which the verifier does not see." Plain text, no banned words.

In reader_brief, after `writeln!(out, "\n{CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE}\n")` and before the `if !inputs.verifier_can_run.is_empty()` block, add a section `# Checkable criteria` holding the const and: "Write each criterion so its check names a file, a diff line or a command the verifier can run (listed under What the verifier can run when given)." It must not refer to a list that may be absent. Do not touch existing lines.

Add `fn checkable_evidence_section() -> String` with heading `## Make your evidence checkable`: the const, then "Prefer a test in your change that shows the property. Add a new file for evidence only when a deliverable or a criterion names it. If a criterion can be shown only from your report, say in its criteria_check entry that the verifier cannot check it; do not invent a file." Do not use the word commit. Call it in producer_brief_with_evidence with `let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", checkable_evidence_section());` just before `criteria_check_section(&mut out, &inputs.reading)` (~686).

Add test `the_reader_brief_requires_criteria_checkable_from_the_snapshot`: render `reader_brief(&reader_inputs(&reading()))`; assert it contains the literals `# Checkable criteria`, `checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs` and `producer's report or change description`; assert the index of `# Checkable criteria` is below the index of `# What the verifier can run`.

Add test `producer_brief_requires_checkable_evidence_in_the_snapshot`: build ProducerInputs as in `producer_briefs_say_what_the_verifier_can_see` (~2710); assert the heading `## Make your evidence checkable`, the same rule literal, `a test in your change`, `only when a deliverable or a criterion names it`, `the verifier cannot check it`; assert the text `you commit` is absent; assert the heading index is below that of `## criteria_check: copy the line`; assert `LEFT_TO_ATHENA` text still appears.

In structure-pass.md section 5 (lines 215-294): add a one-sentence opening note that no item rests on the producer's report or change description, because the verifier sees neither. Rewrite item 2 to say the verifier reruns `cargo test --locked -p athena-core -- --list` on the candidate and item 1's diff check (no test line removed or added except `use`) shows the names unchanged. Rewrite item 3 so every line not marked moved in `git diff -M --color-moved=zebra` must be a `mod`, `use`, `pub use` or visibility line, read from the diff. Rewrite item 5 so the verifier reruns the Grep for each moved name's old path over `crates/` on the candidate, `git diff -U0 -- crates/` shows no line with an old path removed or added outside moved blocks, every hit compiles, and for fake hosts implementing `PrHost` the test named in 5.1 is run by name; add no note or file. Rewrite the two R5-R8 bullets: the diff shows each removed `return Ok(closing)` with a `Flow::Stop` added in its place, counted from `git diff`, and every local that crossed a seam appears as a named field in the diff. Rewrite the 5.2 sentences: the verifier runs the committed guard self-tests in external_calls_guard.rs on the candidate and reruns the Grep; the test that a landing touching a moved file still selects D87 and D88 is committed in the job. Update the 5.1 R5-R8 row to say the early-return pairing is read in the diff. Leave G1-G8 and R1-R9 rows and numbering untouched. Then Grep `report` over section 5 and fix any hit that remains.

Add one line under `### Added` of `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md (line 8, 10): the reader and producer briefs require every criterion to be checkable from the snapshot, diff or verifier commands, and structure-pass section 5 puts its evidence in the snapshot or in commands the verifier reruns.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Run `git diff --stat` and `git status` and confirm only the three files changed, with nothing under crates/athena-context/prompts and no new file.

risks.risk: The rules-section length test (<2600 bytes) or the rule count test breaks if the rule lands in the rules section.
risks.mitigation: The reader section has its own `# ` heading after the rules section, so the `split("\n# ")` slicing in existing tests excludes it; run cargo test -p athena-context.

risks.risk: A producer-brief test compares exact full text or section order.
risks.mitigation: Keep the producer section short; the new test asserts presence and relative order only; run the full cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: The doc edit drifts into the moves G1-G8 and R1-R9 (out of scope).
risks.mitigation: Rewrite only evidence sentences in section 5 and the 5.1 R5-R8 row; keep numbering and the move rows; confirm the diff shows no change outside section 5 and row 294.

risks.risk: A rewritten item lowers the strength of its check (for example item 2 loses its count).
risks.mitigation: Each replacement is a command the verifier runs itself (`--list` on the candidate, the old-path Grep on the candidate) plus a diff check (no test line removed, no old-path hit line changed), which is checkable and at least as strong as a count in a report.

risks.risk: New text trips the boundary-word scan.
risks.mitigation: Avoid the listed words and write no email-like text; the policy test runs in cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: The producer reads the new section as forbidding criteria_check evidence in its report.
risks.mitigation: The text says the report is still where it states what it ran or read; it only says criteria must be checkable by the verifier and that report-only proof must be flagged as uncheckable.

risks.risk: The producer edits a file beyond the three (a prompt file, checks.rs, or a new evidence file).
risks.mitigation: Criterion 6's `git diff --stat` and `git status`, and step 9, catch it; the plan places all text in Rust-built briefs and adds no evidence file.
